### Defensive fit and roster-disruption read (qualitative; video / Synergy only)

<!--
  WHY THIS SECTION: the open-data framework (R/01-14) is OFFENSE-ONLY. The open
  PBP has no matchup, tracking, defender, or screen data, so a defensive read
  cannot be quantified from it. Defense enters the framework HERE, qualitatively,
  from film and Synergy team-aggregate context, quarantined and cited like all
  Synergy content. Keep it to the case-study teams (GSV, TOR, PDX); do not build
  a league-wide defensive table. The reproducible quantitative versions of these
  ideas (box-defense screen, usage/disruption fit-cost, lineup flexibility) are
  the v2 roadmap in PLAN.md, not this cycle.

  Address, for each named candidate, only the items the film actually supports:
  - Switchability / matchup versatility: can she credibly guard more than one
    position; does she let the defense switch ball screens without a mismatch.
  - Defensive athleticism: length, foot speed, lateral quickness, recovery.
    Especially valuable for a big or a bigger guard who can cover multiple spots.
  - Off-ball and screen-navigation context around an offensive player: screen
    assists, gravity, cutting, and screening work that box scores never capture.
    Use this to add texture to an offensive player, not to invent a stat.
  - Second-unit stabilization: does she hold up when the starters sit, so the
    bench minutes stop leaking (the mentor's point that this is where a defensive
    add pays off most).
  - Defensive pace / activity fit: can she play at the team's pace on both ends;
    active hands and defensive-rebound reliability against the shot types this
    team's identity concedes (e.g. cleaning midrange misses for a midrange-heavy,
    transition-heavy opponent).
  - Roster-disruption cost: does adding this player DEMAND the ball or shot
    volume, and would that disrupt the acquiring team's shot allocation and
    hierarchy. The low-disruption defensive add (improves defense without
    demanding usage) is the easy win; flag high-usage adds as an offensive cost.

  Every Synergy-sourced number carries: "Source: Synergy Sports | 2026 WNBA".
  If a claim rests on film judgment rather than a cited number, say so plainly.
-->
